passages.text: Then the whole council rose and led Jesus away to Pilate.
passages.sermon: The whole council stood up.\r\nThey led Jesus away.\r\nThey took Him to Pilate.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναστὰν ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος αὐτῶν ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Πιλᾶτον

passages.text: And they began to accuse Him, saying, “We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding payment of taxes to Caesar, and proclaiming Himself to be Christ, a King.”
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders began to accuse Jesus.
They spoke to Pilate.
They said, “We found this man causing trouble in our nation.”
They said, “He tells people not to pay taxes to Caesar.”
They said, “He claims to be Christ, a King.”
passages.original: ἤρξαντο δὲ κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Τοῦτον εὕραμεν διαστρέφοντα τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ κωλύοντα φόρους Καίσαρι διδόναι καὶ λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν Χριστὸν βασιλέα εἶναι

passages.text: So Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to Jesus.
Pilate asked Jesus a question.
Pilate said, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered Pilate.
Jesus said, “You have said so.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν λέγων Σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ ἔφη Σὺ λέγεις

passages.text: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the crowds, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
passages.sermon: Pilate was the Roman governor.\r\nHe spoke to the chief priests and the crowds.\r\nHe said, “I find no basis for a charge against this man.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους Οὐδὲν εὑρίσκω αἴτιον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ

passages.text: But they kept insisting, “He stirs up the people all over Judea with His teaching. He began in Galilee and has come all the way here.”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the crowds spoke to Pilate.
They insisted on their accusation against Jesus.
They said Jesus stirs up the people.
They said He teaches throughout all Judea.
They said He began His teaching in Galilee.
They said He has come all the way to this place.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπίσχυον λέγοντες ὅτι Ἀνασείει τὸν λαὸν διδάσκων καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἕως ὧδε

passages.text: When Pilate heard this, he asked if the man was a Galilean.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate heard the accusation against Jesus.
The accusers said Jesus stirred up the people from Galilee to Judea.
Pilate asked a question.
He asked if Jesus was a Galilean.
passages.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ ἀκούσας ἐπηρώτησεν εἰ ὁ ἄνθρωπος Γαλιλαῖός ἐστιν

passages.text: And learning that Jesus was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent Him to Herod, who himself was in Jerusalem at that time.
passages.sermon: Pilate learned that Jesus was under Herod’s authority.\r\nPilate sent Jesus to Herod.\r\nHerod was in Jerusalem at that time.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπιγνοὺς ὅτι ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας Ἡρῴδου ἐστὶν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν πρὸς Ἡρῴδην ὄντα καὶ αὐτὸν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐν ταύταις ταῖς ἡμέραις

passages.text: When Herod saw Jesus, he was greatly pleased. He had wanted to see Him for a long time, because he had heard about Him and was hoping to see Him perform a miracle.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a ruler in Jerusalem at that time.
Herod saw Jesus.
Herod felt very happy.
Herod had wanted to see Jesus for a long time.
Herod had heard about Jesus.
Herod hoped to see Jesus perform a miracle.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἡρῴδης ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐχάρη λίαν ἦν γὰρ ἐξ ἱκανῶν χρόνων θέλων ἰδεῖν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ ἀκούειν περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλπιζέν τι σημεῖον ἰδεῖν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ γινόμενον

passages.text: Herod questioned Jesus at great length, but He gave no answer.
passages.sermon: Herod was the ruler of Galilee.\r\nHerod questioned Jesus for a long time.\r\nJesus did not answer Herod at all.
passages.original: ἐπηρώτα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐν λόγοις ἱκανοῖς αὐτὸς δὲ οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτῷ

passages.text: Meanwhile, the chief priests and scribes stood there, vehemently accusing Him.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests stood there.
The scribes stood there.
They accused Jesus.
They accused Him with strong words.
They spoke against Him with great intensity.
passages.original: Εἱστήκεισαν δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς εὐτόνως κατηγοροῦντες αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And even Herod and his soldiers ridiculed and mocked Him. Dressing Him in a fine robe, they sent Him back to Pilate.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a ruler in Jerusalem.
Herod had soldiers with him.
Herod and his soldiers ridiculed Jesus.
They mocked Jesus.
They put a fine robe on Jesus.
They sent Jesus back to Pilate.
passages.original: ἐξουθενήσας δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ ὁ Ἡρῴδης σὺν τοῖς στρατεύμασιν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐμπαίξας περιβαλὼν ἐσθῆτα λαμπρὰν ἀνέπεμψεν αὐτὸν τῷ Πιλάτῳ

passages.text: That day Herod and Pilate became friends; before this time they had been enemies.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a ruler in Judea.
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Herod and Pilate had been enemies before.
They did not get along with each other.
On that day, Herod and Pilate became friends.
They changed from being enemies to being friends.
passages.original: Ἐγένοντο δὲ φίλοι ὅ τε Ἡρῴδης καὶ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ μετ’ ἀλλήλων προϋπῆρχον γὰρ ἐν ἔχθρᾳ ὄντες πρὸς αὑτούς

passages.text: Then Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people, and said to them, “You brought me this man as one who was inciting the people to rebellion. I have examined Him here in your presence and found Him not guilty of your charges against Him.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate called together the chief priests.
He called the rulers.
He called the people.
Pilate spoke to them.
He said, “You brought this man to me.
You said He was turning the people away.
I have questioned Him in front of you.
I have found nothing wrong in this man.
He is not guilty of the charges you bring against Him.”
passages.original: Πιλᾶτος δὲ συνκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τὸν λαὸν εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Προσηνέγκατέ μοι τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦτον ὡς ἀποστρέφοντα τὸν λαόν καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ἀνακρίνας οὐθὲν εὗρον ἐν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τούτῳ αἴτιον ὧν κατηγορεῖτε κατ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Neither has Herod, for he sent Him back to us. As you can see, He has done nothing deserving of death.
passages.sermon:
Herod also did not find Him guilty.
Herod sent Him back to us.
He has done nothing that deserves death.
You can see this for yourselves.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ Ἡρῴδης ἀνέπεμψεν γὰρ αὐτὸν πρὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ ἰδοὺ οὐδὲν ἄξιον θανάτου ἐστὶν πεπραγμένον αὐτῷ

passages.text: Therefore I will punish Him and release Him.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd.
Pilate said he would punish Jesus.
Pilate said he would then release Jesus.
passages.original: παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω

passages.text: But they all cried out in unison: “Away with this man! Release Barabbas to us!”
passages.sermon:
A large crowd stood together.
They all shouted at the same time.
They said, “Take this man away!”
They said, “Release Barabbas to us!”
passages.original: Ἀνέκραγον δὲ παμπληθεὶ λέγοντες Αἶρε τοῦτον ἀπόλυσον δὲ ἡμῖν τὸν Βαραββᾶν

passages.text: (Barabbas had been imprisoned for an insurrection in the city, and for murder.)
passages.sermon:
Barabbas was a prisoner.
Authorities had arrested Barabbas.
He had caused an insurrection in the city.
He had committed murder.
They put Barabbas in prison for these crimes.
passages.original: ὅστις ἦν διὰ στάσιν τινὰ γενομένην ἐν τῇ πόλει καὶ φόνον βληθεὶς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ

passages.text: Wanting to release Jesus, Pilate addressed them again, but they kept shouting, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate wanted to release Jesus.
Pilate spoke to the crowd again.
The crowd shouted loudly.
They said, “Crucify Him! Crucify Him!”
passages.original: Πάλιν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος προσεφώνησεν αὐτοῖς θέλων ἀπολῦσαι τὸν Ἰησοῦν οἱ δὲ ἐπεφώνουν λέγοντες Σταύρου σταύρου αὐτόν

passages.text: A third time he said to them, “What evil has this man done? I have found in Him no offense worthy of death. So after I punish Him, I will release Him.”
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
Pilate spoke to the crowd for the third time.
Pilate asked them, "What evil has this man done?"
Pilate said, "I have found no offense in him that deserves death."
Pilate said, "I will punish him."
Pilate said, "Then I will release him."
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ τρίτον εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος οὐδὲν αἴτιον θανάτου εὗρον ἐν αὐτῷ παιδεύσας οὖν αὐτὸν ἀπολύσω

passages.text: But they were insistent, demanding with loud voices for Jesus to be crucified. And their clamor prevailed.
passages.sermon:
The crowd spoke with loud voices.
They demanded that Jesus be crucified.
They insisted strongly.
Their loud demands became stronger than any opposition.
Their voices prevailed.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ἐπέκειντο φωναῖς μεγάλαις αἰτούμενοι αὐτὸν σταυρωθῆναι καὶ κατίσχυον αἱ φωναὶ αὐτῶν

passages.text: So Pilate sentenced that their demand be met.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The crowd demanded that Jesus be crucified.
Pilate decided to grant their request.
He gave the order for their demand to be carried out.
passages.original: καὶ Πιλᾶτος ἐπέκρινεν γενέσθαι τὸ αἴτημα αὐτῶν

passages.text: As they had requested, he released the one imprisoned for insurrection and murder, and handed Jesus over to their will.
passages.sermon:
Pilate was the Roman governor.
The crowd asked Pilate to release a prisoner.
This prisoner was in jail for insurrection and murder.
Pilate released this man, as the crowd requested.
Pilate handed Jesus over to the will of the crowd.
passages.original: ἀπέλυσεν δὲ τὸν διὰ στάσιν καὶ φόνον βεβλημένον εἰς φυλακὴν ὃν ᾐτοῦντο τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν παρέδωκεν τῷ θελήματι αὐτῶν

passages.text: As the soldiers led Him away, they seized Simon of Cyrene on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers led Jesus away.
They saw Simon.
Simon came from Cyrene.
Simon was coming in from the country.
The soldiers seized Simon.
They put the cross on Simon.
They made Simon carry the cross behind Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ ὡς ἀπήγαγον αὐτόν ἐπιλαβόμενοι Σίμωνά τινα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ ἐπέθηκαν αὐτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν φέρειν ὄπισθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus walked toward His crucifixion.
A large crowd followed Jesus.
Many women were in the crowd.
The women mourned for Jesus.
The women wailed for Jesus.
passages.original: Ἠκολούθει δὲ αὐτῷ πολὺ πλῆθος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ γυναικῶν αἳ ἐκόπτοντο καὶ ἐθρήνουν αὐτόν

passages.text: But Jesus turned to them and said, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me, but weep for yourselves and for your children.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was walking to be crucified.
Many people followed Him.
Many women mourned and wailed for Him.
Jesus turned to these women.
He spoke to them directly.
He said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me.
Weep for yourselves.
Weep for your children."
passages.original: στραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς αὐτὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Θυγατέρες Ἰερουσαλήμ μὴ κλαίετε ἐπ’ ἐμέ πλὴν ἐφ’ ἑαυτὰς κλαίετε καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ὑμῶν

passages.text: Look, the days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that never bore, and breasts that never nursed!’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the women of Jerusalem.
He warned them about the future.
He said, “The days are coming.
In those days, people will speak.
They will say, ‘Blessed are the women who cannot have children.
Blessed are the wombs that never gave birth.
Blessed are the breasts that never nursed a child.’”
passages.original: ὅτι ἰδοὺ ἔρχονται ἡμέραι ἐν αἷς ἐροῦσιν Μακάριαι αἱ στεῖραι καὶ αἱ κοιλίαι αἳ οὐκ ἐγέννησαν καὶ μαστοὶ οἳ οὐκ ἔθρεψαν

passages.text: At that time ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!” and to the hills, “Cover us!” ’
passages.sermon:
People will face great trouble.
At that time, they will speak to the mountains.
They will say, “Fall on us!”
They will speak to the hills.
They will say, “Cover us!”
passages.original: τότε Ἄρξονται λέγειν τοῖς ὄρεσιν Πέσετε ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς Καὶ τοῖς βουνοῖς Καλύψατε ἡμᾶς

passages.text: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus warned them about coming judgment.
He said, “If people do these things when the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”
People act this way now, while there is still hope and life.
It will be worse when hope is gone and judgment comes.
passages.original: Ὅτι εἰ ἐν τῷ ὑγρῷ ξύλῳ ταῦτα ποιοῦσιν ἐν τῷ ξηρῷ τί γένηται

passages.text: Two others, who were criminals, were also led away to be executed with Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers led Jesus away to be executed.
They also led two other men with Him.
These two men were criminals.
All three were going to be executed together.
passages.original: Ἤγοντο δὲ καὶ ἕτεροι κακοῦργοι δύο σὺν αὐτῷ ἀναιρεθῆναι

passages.text: When they came to the place called The Skull, they crucified Him there, along with the criminals, one on His right and the other on His left.
passages.sermon:
Jesus went with others to a place called The Skull.
The people brought Jesus there.
They crucified Jesus at that place.
They also crucified two criminals with Him.
One criminal was on His right side.
The other criminal was on His left side.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον τὸν καλούμενον Κρανίον ἐκεῖ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς κακούργους ὃν μὲν ἐκ δεξιῶν ὃν δὲ ἐξ ἀριστερῶν

passages.text: Then Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided up His garments by casting lots.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was being crucified.
He spoke to God the Father.
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them.”
He said, “They do not know what they are doing.”
The soldiers took Jesus’ clothes.
They divided His garments among themselves.
They cast lots to decide who would get each piece.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν Πάτερ ἄφες αὐτοῖς οὐ γὰρ οἴδασιν τί ποιοῦσιν διαμεριζόμενοι δὲ τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἔβαλον κλήρους

passages.text: The people stood watching, and the rulers sneered at Him, saying, “He saved others; let Him save Himself if He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
The people stood there.
They watched Him.
The rulers were also there.
The rulers sneered at Jesus.
They spoke to each other about Him.
They said, “He saved other people.”
They said, “Let Him save Himself.”
They said, “If He is the Christ of God, the Chosen One, He should save Himself.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἱστήκει ὁ λαὸς θεωρῶν ἐξεμυκτήριζον δὲ καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες λέγοντες Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν σωσάτω ἑαυτόν εἰ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ ὁ ἐκλεκτός

passages.text: The soldiers also mocked Him and came up to offer Him sour wine.
passages.sermon:
Roman soldiers stood near Jesus.
They mocked Jesus.
They walked up to Him.
They offered Him sour wine.
passages.original: Ἐνέπαιξαν δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ στρατιῶται προσερχόμενοι ὄξος προσφέροντες αὐτῷ

passages.text: “If You are the King of the Jews,” they said, “save Yourself!”
passages.sermon: The soldiers mocked Jesus.\r\nThey spoke to Him.\r\nThey said, “If You are the King of the Jews, save Yourself.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγοντες Εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων σῶσον σεαυτόν

passages.text: Above Him was posted an inscription: THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was crucified.
\r\nThe soldiers mocked Jesus.
\r\nThey offered Him sour wine.
\r\nThey called Him the King of the Jews.
\r\nSomeone placed a sign above Jesus.
\r\nThe sign said, "THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS."
passages.original: Ἦν δὲ καὶ ἐπιγραφὴ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ Ο ΒΑΣΙΛΕΥΣ ΤΩΝ ΙΟΥΔΑΙΩΝ ΟΥΤΟΣ

passages.text: One of the criminals who hung there heaped abuse on Him. “Are You not the Christ?” he said. “Save Yourself and us!”
passages.sermon:
One criminal hung on a cross beside Jesus.
This criminal was guilty of wrongdoing.
He insulted Jesus.
He spoke to Jesus.
He said, “Are you not the Christ?”
He said, “Save yourself and us!”
passages.original: Εἷς δὲ τῶν κρεμασθέντων κακούργων ἐβλασφήμει αὐτόν λέγων Οὐχὶ σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός σῶσον σεαυτὸν καὶ ἡμᾶς

passages.text: But the other one rebuked him, saying, “Do you not even fear God, since you are under the same judgment?
passages.sermon:
Two criminals hung beside Jesus.
One criminal insulted Jesus.
The other criminal spoke to him.
He rebuked the first criminal.
He said, “Do you not fear God?”
He said, “You are under the same judgment.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἕτερος ἐπιτιμῶν αὐτῷ ἔφη Οὐδὲ φοβῇ σὺ τὸν Θεόν ὅτι ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ κρίματι εἶ

passages.text: We are punished justly, for we are receiving what our actions deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
passages.sermon:
Two criminals hung on crosses beside Jesus.
One criminal spoke to the other.
He said, “We are punished justly.”
He meant, “We deserve our punishment.”
He said, “We are receiving what our actions deserve.”
He looked at Jesus.
He said, “But this man has done nothing wrong.”
passages.original: καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν δικαίως ἄξια γὰρ ὧν ἐπράξαμεν ἀπολαμβάνομεν οὗτος δὲ οὐδὲν ἄτοπον ἔπραξεν

passages.text: Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when You come into Your kingdom!”
passages.sermon: One of the criminals spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said, “Jesus, remember me.”\r\nHe asked Jesus to remember him when Jesus came into His kingdom.
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ἰησοῦ μνήσθητί μου ὅταν ἔλθῃς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν σου

passages.text: And Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you, today you will be with Me in Paradise.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the man next to Him on the cross.\r\nJesus said, “Truly, I tell you this now.\r\nToday you will be with Me in Paradise.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀμήν σοι λέγω σήμερον μετ’ ἐμοῦ ἔσῃ ἐν τῷ Παραδείσῳ

passages.text: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
passages.sermon: It was about the sixth hour.\r\nDarkness came over all the land.\r\nThis darkness lasted until the ninth hour.
passages.original: Καὶ ἦν ἤδη ὡσεὶ ὥρα ἕκτη καὶ σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης

passages.text: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
passages.sermon: The sun became dark.\r\nThe veil in the temple tore in the middle.
passages.original: τοῦ ἡλίου ἐκλιπόντος ἐσχίσθη δὲ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ μέσον

passages.text: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was on the cross.
He spoke in a loud voice.
He said, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.”
After Jesus said this, He breathed His last.
Jesus died.
passages.original: Καὶ φωνήσας φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Πάτερ εἰς χεῖράς σου παρατίθεμαι τὸ πνεῦμά μου τοῦτο δὲ εἰπὼν ἐξέπνευσεν

passages.text: When the centurion saw what had happened, he gave glory to God, saying, “Surely this was a righteous man.”
passages.sermon:
A Roman centurion stood near the cross.
He saw everything that happened when Jesus died.
He saw the sun grow dark.
He saw the temple veil tear in two.
He saw Jesus call out to God and die.
The centurion gave glory to God.
He said, “Surely this man was righteous.”
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης τὸ γενόμενον ἐδόξαζεν τὸν Θεὸν λέγων Ὄντως ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος δίκαιος ἦν

passages.text: And when all the people who had gathered for this spectacle saw what had happened, they returned home beating their breasts.
passages.sermon:
Many people gathered to watch what happened to Jesus.
These people saw everything that took place.
They felt deep sorrow.
They beat their chests.
They went back to their homes.
passages.original: καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαραγενόμενοι ὄχλοι ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν ταύτην θεωρήσαντες τὰ γενόμενα τύπτοντες τὰ στήθη ὑπέστρεφον

passages.text: But all those who knew Jesus, including the women who had followed Him from Galilee, stood at a distance watching these things.
passages.sermon: All the people who knew Jesus stood far away.\r\nThe women who had followed Jesus from Galilee also stood there.\r\nThey watched everything that happened.
passages.original: εἱστήκεισαν δὲ πάντες οἱ γνωστοὶ αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ γυναῖκες αἱ συνακολουθοῦσαι αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ὁρῶσαι ταῦτα

passages.text: Now there was a Council member named Joseph, a good and righteous man, who had not consented to their decision or action. He was from the Judean town of Arimathea, and was waiting for the kingdom of God.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a member of the Council.
Joseph was a good man.
Joseph was a righteous man.
Joseph did not agree with the Council’s decision.
Joseph did not agree with the Council’s action.
Joseph came from Arimathea, a town in Judea.
Joseph was waiting for the kingdom of God.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι Ἰωσὴφ βουλευτὴς ὑπάρχων καὶ ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ δίκαιος οὗτος οὐκ ἦν συνκατατεθειμένος τῇ βουλῇ καὶ τῇ πράξει αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας πόλεως τῶν Ἰουδαίων ὃς προσεδέχετο τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: He went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a member of the Council.
Joseph was a good and righteous man.
Joseph had not agreed with the Council’s decision or action.
Joseph came from the Judean town of Arimathea.
Joseph was waiting for the kingdom of God.
Joseph went to Pilate.
Joseph asked Pilate for the body of Jesus.
passages.original: οὗτος προσελθὼν τῷ Πιλάτῳ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: Then he took it down, wrapped it in a linen cloth, and placed it in a tomb cut into the rock, where no one had yet been laid.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a good and righteous man from Arimathea.
He was a member of the Council.
He did not agree with their decision or action.
He waited for the kingdom of God.
Joseph went to Pilate.
He asked for the body of Jesus.
Joseph took the body of Jesus down from the cross.
He wrapped the body in a linen cloth.
He placed the body in a tomb cut into the rock.
No one had ever been laid in that tomb before.
passages.original: καὶ καθελὼν ἐνετύλιξεν αὐτὸ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνήματι λαξευτῷ οὗ οὐκ ἦν οὐδεὶς οὔπω κείμενος

passages.text: It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was beginning.
passages.sermon: This happened on Preparation Day.\r\nThe Sabbath was about to begin.
passages.original: καὶ ἡμέρα ἦν Παρασκευῆς καὶ σάββατον ἐπέφωσκεν

passages.text: The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed, and they saw the tomb and how His body was placed.
passages.sermon:
Some women had come with Jesus from Galilee.
These women followed.
They saw the tomb.
They saw how people placed Jesus’ body in the tomb.
passages.original: Κατακολουθήσασαι δὲ αἱ γυναῖκες αἵτινες ἦσαν συνεληλυθυῖαι ἐκ τῆς Γαλιλαίας αὐτῷ ἐθεάσαντο τὸ μνημεῖον καὶ ὡς ἐτέθη τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Then they returned to prepare spices and perfumes. And they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment.
passages.sermon:
The women had come with Jesus from Galilee.
They returned from the tomb.
They prepared spices.
They prepared perfumes.
They rested on the Sabbath.
They obeyed the commandment.
passages.original: ὑποστρέψασαι δὲ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα καὶ μύρα Καὶ τὸ μὲν σάββατον ἡσύχασαν κατὰ τὴν ἐντολήν
